function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

   17|     (r'(--|# )\+.*?(\r\n|\r|\n|$)', tokens.Comment.Single.Hint),
   18|     (r'/\*\+[\s\S]*?\*/', tokens.Comment.Multiline.Hint),
   19| 
   20|     (r'(--|# ).*?(\r\n|\r|\n|$)', tokens.Comment.Single),
   21|     (r'/\*[\s\S]*?\*/', tokens.Comment.Multiline),
   22| 
   23|     (r'(\r\n|\r|\n)', tokens.Newline),
   24|     (r'\s+?', tokens.Whitespace),
   25| 
   26|     (r':=', tokens.Assignment),
   27|     (r'::', tokens.Punctuation),
   28| 
   29|     (r'\*', tokens.Wildcard),
   30| 
   31|     (r"`(``|[^`])*`", tokens.Name),
   32|     (r"´(´´|[^´])*´", tokens.Name),
   33|     (r'((?<![\w\"\$])\$(?:[_A-ZÀ-Ü]\w*)?\$)[\s\S]*?\1', tokens.Literal),
   34| 
   35|     (r'\?', tokens.Name.Placeholder),
   36|     (r'%(\(\w+\))?s', tokens.Name.Placeholder),
   37|     (r'(?<!\w)[$:?]\w+', tokens.Name.Placeholder),
   38| 
   39|     (r'\\\w+', tokens.Command),
   40| 
   41|     # FIXME(andi): VALUES shouldn't be listed here
   42|     # see https://github.com/andialbrecht/sqlparse/pull/64
   43|     # AS and IN are special, it may be followed by a parenthesis, but
   44|     # are never functions, see issue183 and issue507
   45|     (r'(CASE|IN|VALUES|USING|FROM|AS)\b', tokens.Keyword),
   46| 
   47|     (r'(@|##|#)[A-ZÀ-Ü]\w+', tokens.Name),
   48| 
   49|     # see issue #39
   50|     # Spaces around period `schema . name` are valid identifier
   51|     # TODO: Spaces before period not implemented
   52|     (r'[A-ZÀ-Ü]\w*(?=\s*\.)', tokens.Name),  # 'Name'.
   53|     # FIXME(atronah): never match,
   54|     # because `re.match` doesn't work with look-behind regexp feature
   55|     (r'(?<=\.)[A-ZÀ-Ü]\w*', tokens.Name),  # .'Name'
   56|     (r'[A-ZÀ-Ü]\w*(?=\()', tokens.Name),  # side effect: change kw to func
   57|     (r'-?0x[\dA-F]+', tokens.Number.Hexadecimal),
   58|     (r'-?\d+(\.\d+)?E-?\d+', tokens.Number.Float),
   59|     (r'(?![_A-ZÀ-Ü])-?(\d+(\.\d*)|\.\d+)(?![_A-ZÀ-Ü])',
   60|      tokens.Number.Float),
   61|     (r'(?![_A-ZÀ-Ü])-?\d+(?![_A-ZÀ-Ü])', tokens.Number.Integer),
   62|     (r"'(''|\\'|[^'])*'", tokens.String.Single),
   63|     # not a real string literal in ANSI SQL:
   64|     (r'"(""|\\"|[^"])*"', tokens.String.Symbol),
   65|     (r'(""|".*?[^\\]")', tokens.String.Symbol),
   66|     # sqlite names can be escaped with [square brackets]. left bracket
   67|     # cannot be preceded by word character or a right bracket --
   68|     # otherwise it's probably an array index
   69|     (r'(?<![\w\])])(\[[^\]\[]+\])', tokens.Name),
   70|     (r'((LEFT\s+|RIGHT\s+|FULL\s+)?(INNER\s+|OUTER\s+|STRAIGHT\s+)?'
   71|      r'|(CROSS\s+|NATURAL\s+)?)?JOIN\b', tokens.Keyword),
   72|     (r'END(\s+IF|\s+LOOP|\s+WHILE|\s+FOR|\s+CASE)?\b', tokens.Keyword),
   73|     (r'IF\s+(NOT\s+)?EXISTS\b', tokens.Keyword),
   74|     (r'NOT\s+NULL\b', tokens.Keyword),
   75|     (r'(ASC|DESC)(\s+NULLS\s+(FIRST|LAST))?\b', tokens.Keyword.Order),
   76|     (r'(ASC|DESC)\b', tokens.Keyword.Order),
   77|     (r'NULLS\s+(FIRST|LAST)\b', tokens.Keyword.Order),
   78|     (r'UNION\s+ALL\b', tokens.Keyword),
   79|     (r'CREATE(\s+OR\s+REPLACE)?\b', tokens.Keyword.DDL),
   80|     (r'DOUBLE\s+PRECISION\b', tokens.Name.Builtin),
   81|     (r'GROUP\s+BY\b', tokens.Keyword),
   82|     (r'ORDER\s+BY\b', tokens.Keyword),
   83|     (r'PRIMARY\s+KEY\b', tokens.Keyword),
   84|     (r'HANDLER\s+FOR\b', tokens.Keyword),
   85|     (r'GO(\s\d+)\b', tokens.Keyword),
   86|     (r'(LATERAL\s+VIEW\s+)'
   87|      r'(EXPLODE|INLINE|PARSE_URL_TUPLE|POSEXPLODE|STACK)\b',
   88|      tokens.Keyword),
   89|     (r"(AT|WITH')\s+TIME\s+ZONE\s+'[^']+'", tokens.Keyword.TZCast),
   90|     (r'(NOT\s+)?(LIKE|ILIKE|RLIKE)\b', tokens.Operator.Comparison),
   91|     (r'(NOT\s+)?(REGEXP)(\s+(BINARY))?\b', tokens.Operator.Comparison),
   92|     # Check for keywords, also returns tokens.Name if regex matches
   93|     # but the match isn't a keyword.
   94|     (r'\w[$#\w]*', PROCESS_AS_KEYWORD),
   95|     (r'[;:()\[\],\.]', tokens.Punctuation),
   96|     # JSON operators
   97|     (r'(\->>?|#>>?|@>|<@|\?\|?|\?&|\-|#\-)', tokens.Operator),
   98|     (r'[<>=~!]+', tokens.Operator.Comparison),
   99|     (r'[+/@#%^&|^-]+', tokens.Operator),

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note

function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

Found the root cause: in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's _change_splitlevel, the parenthesis handling got inverted. The code decreases _parenthesis_level/level for any punctuation that is NOT ')' (e.g. ';', ',', '.', '[', ']'), but never decreases it for ')' itself, since ')' falls through the `value != ')'` condition into the "ttype not in Keyword" branch returning 0. This means that after the first '(' ... ')' pair is seen, the overall split level never returns to 0, so later top-level semicolons stop splitting statements (self.level stays > 0 forever). That matches the described regression: statements with a parenthesis (e.g. function signatures `func(int)`, dollar-quoted plpgsql bodies with `(int)` parameter lists) silently merge into a single statement instead of splitting at each semicolon, causing counts like "assert 1 == 2" (expected 2 statements, got 1).

I'll fix the condition to only decrease the level when value == ')' (restoring correct open/close paren matching), then verify with repro scripts.

Found the root cause: in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's _change_splitlevel, the parenthesis handling got inverted. The code decreases _parenthesis_level/level for any punctuation that is NOT ')' (e.g. ';', ',', '.', '[', ']'), but never decreases it for ')' itself, since ')' falls through the `value != ')'` condition into the "ttype not in Keyword" branch returning 0. This means that after the first '(' ... ')' pair is seen, the overall split level never returns to 0, so later top-level semicolons stop splitting statements (self.level stays > 0 forever). That matches the described regression: statements with a parenthesis (e.g. function signatures `func(int)`, dollar-quoted plpgsql bodies with `(int)` parameter lists) silently merge into a single statement instead of splitting at each semicolon, causing counts like "assert 1 == 2" (expected 2 statements, got 1).

I'll fix the condition to only decrease the level when value == ')' (restoring correct open/close paren matching), then verify with repro scripts.

Found the root cause: in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's _change_splitlevel, the parenthesis handling got inverted. The code decreases _parenthesis_level/level for any punctuation that is NOT ')' (e.g. ';', ',', '.', '[', ']'), but never decreases it for ')' itself, since ')' falls through the `value != ')'` condition into the "ttype not in Keyword" branch returning 0. This means that after the first '(' ... ')' pair is seen, the overall split level never returns to 0, so later top-level semicolons stop splitting statements (self.level stays > 0 forever). That matches the described regression: statements with a parenthesis (e.g. function signatures `func(int)`, dollar-quoted plpgsql bodies with `(int)` parameter lists) silently merge into a single statement instead of splitting at each semicolon, causing counts like "assert 1 == 2" (expected 2 statements, got 1).

I'll fix the condition to only decrease the level when value == ')' (restoring correct open/close paren matching), then verify with repro scripts.

The regression was a bug in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's `_change_splitlevel`: the condition for decreasing the parenthesis/split level checked `value != ')'` instead of `value == ')'`. This meant a closing `)` never decremented the level (it fell through to the "not a keyword" branch returning 0), while every other punctuation token (like `;`, `,`, `.`) incorrectly decremented it. Once any `(...)` pair appeared (e.g. a function parameter list `func(int)`), the split level stayed permanently elevated, so subsequent top-level semicolons no longer caused statement splitting — multiple statements got merged into one. This explains the "psql quotation marks", "issue83" (dollar-quoted function bodies with parens), and "issue193 splitting function" failures, plus the other affected cases.

Fixed by changing the elif condition from `value != ')'` to `value == ')'` so parenthesis level only decreases on an actual closing parenthesis. Verified via a repro script that: two simple statements still split correctly, comments still split correctly, dollar-quoted CREATE FUNCTION bodies (with parens in signatures) now split into 2 statements instead of merging into 1, and DECLARE-based splitting still works as before (3 statements). Now running the full test suite to confirm no other regressions, then cleaning up the temporary repro files.

The regression was a bug in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's `_change_splitlevel`: the condition for decreasing the parenthesis/split level checked `value != ')'` instead of `value == ')'`. This meant a closing `)` never decremented the level (it fell through to the "not a keyword" branch returning 0), while every other punctuation token (like `;`, `,`, `.`) incorrectly decremented it. Once any `(...)` pair appeared (e.g. a function parameter list `func(int)`), the split level stayed permanently elevated, so subsequent top-level semicolons no longer caused statement splitting — multiple statements got merged into one. This explains the "psql quotation marks", "issue83" (dollar-quoted function bodies with parens), and "issue193 splitting function" failures, plus the other affected cases.

Fixed by changing the elif condition from `value != ')'` to `value == ')'` so parenthesis level only decreases on an actual closing parenthesis. Verified via a repro script that: two simple statements still split correctly, comments still split correctly, dollar-quoted CREATE FUNCTION bodies (with parens in signatures) now split into 2 statements instead of merging into 1, and DECLARE-based splitting still works as before (3 statements). Now running the full test suite to confirm no other regressions, then cleaning up the temporary repro files.

Found the root cause: in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's _change_splitlevel, the parenthesis handling got inverted. The code decreases _parenthesis_level/level for any punctuation that is NOT ')' (e.g. ';', ',', '.', '[', ']'), but never decreases it for ')' itself, since ')' falls through the `value != ')'` condition into the "ttype not in Keyword" branch returning 0. This means that after the first '(' ... ')' pair is seen, the overall split level never returns to 0, so later top-level semicolons stop splitting statements (self.level stays > 0 forever). That matches the described regression: statements with a parenthesis (e.g. function signatures `func(int)`, dollar-quoted plpgsql bodies with `(int)` parameter lists) silently merge into a single statement instead of splitting at each semicolon, causing counts like "assert 1 == 2" (expected 2 statements, got 1).

I'll fix the condition to only decrease the level when value == ')' (restoring correct open/close paren matching), then verify with repro scripts.

The regression was a bug in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's `_change_splitlevel`: the condition for decreasing the parenthesis/split level checked `value != ')'` instead of `value == ')'`. This meant a closing `)` never decremented the level (it fell through to the "not a keyword" branch returning 0), while every other punctuation token (like `;`, `,`, `.`) incorrectly decremented it. Once any `(...)` pair appeared (e.g. a function parameter list `func(int)`), the split level stayed permanently elevated, so subsequent top-level semicolons no longer caused statement splitting — multiple statements got merged into one. This explains the "psql quotation marks", "issue83" (dollar-quoted function bodies with parens), and "issue193 splitting function" failures, plus the other affected cases.

Fixed by changing the elif condition from `value != ')'` to `value == ')'` so parenthesis level only decreases on an actual closing parenthesis. The regression was a bug in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's `_change_splitlevel`: the condition for decreasing the parenthesis/split level checked `value != ')'` instead of `value == ')'`. This meant a closing `)` never decremented the level (it fell through to the "not a keyword" branch returning 0), while every other punctuation token (like `;`, `,`, `.`) incorrectly decremented it. Once any `(...)` pair appeared (e.g. a function parameter list `func(int)`), the split level stayed permanently elevated, so subsequent top-level semicolons no longer caused statement splitting — multiple statements got merged into one. This explains the "psql quotation marks", "issue83" (dollar-quoted function bodies with parens), and "issue193 splitting function" failures, plus the other affected cases.

Fixed by changing the elif condition from `value != ')'` to `value == ')'` so parenthesis level only decreases on an actual closing parenthesis. Verified via a repro script that: two simple statements still split correctly, comments still split correctly, dollar-quoted CREATE FUNCTION bodies (with parens in signatures) now split into 2 statements instead of merging into 1, and DECLARE-based splitting still works as before (3 statements). Now running the full test suite to confirm no other regressions, then cleaning up the temporary repro files.

So once any `(...)` pair appeared (e.g. `func(int)` in a CREATE FUNCTION signature), the split level stayed elevated permanently, and subsequent top-level semicolons stopped splitting statements — multiple statements merged into one. Fix: changed the condition to `value == ')'` so the level only decreases on a genuine closing parenthesis, restoring correct paren-level tracking and statement splitting.

Found the root cause: in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's _change_splitlevel, the parenthesis handling got inverted. The code decreases _parenthesis_level/level for any punctuation that is NOT ')' (e.g. ';', ',', '.', '[', ']'), but never decreases it for ')' itself, since ')' falls through the `value != ')'` condition into the "ttype not in Keyword" branch returning 0. This means that after the first '(' ... ')' pair is seen, the overall split level never returns to 0, so later top-level semicolons stop splitting statements (self.level stays > 0 forever). That matches the described regression: statements with a parenthesis (e.g. function signatures `func(int)`, dollar-quoted plpgsql bodies with `(int)` parameter lists) silently merge into a single statement instead of splitting at each semicolon, causing counts like "assert 1 == 2" (expected 2 statements, got 1).

I'll fix the condition to only decrease the level when value == ')' (restoring correct open/close paren matching), then verify with repro scripts.

The regression was a bug in sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py's `_change_splitlevel`: the condition for decreasing the parenthesis/split level checked `value != ')'` instead of `value == ')'`. This meant a closing `)` never decremented the level (it fell through to the "not a keyword" branch returning 0), while every other punctuation token (like `;`, `,`, `.`) incorrectly decremented it. Once any `(...)` pair appeared (e.g. a function parameter list `func(int)`), the split level stayed permanently elevated, so subsequent top-level semicolons no longer caused statement splitting — multiple statements got merged into one. This explains the "psql quotation marks", "issue83" (dollar-quoted function bodies with parens), and "issue193 splitting function" failures, plus the other affected cases.

Fixed by changing the elif condition from `value != ')'` to `value == ')'` so parenthesis level only decreases on an actual closing parenthesis. Verified via a repro script that: two simple statements still split correctly, comments still split correctly, dollar-quoted CREATE FUNCTION bodies (with parens in signatures) now split into 2 statements instead of merging into 1, and DECLARE-based splitting still works as before (3 statements). {"content":"The regression has been fixed and verified. 

Root cause: in `sqlparse/engine/statement_splitter.py`, `_change_splitlevel` decremented the split/parenthesis level for any punctuation token that was *not* a closing parenthesis (`value != ')'`), while an actual closing `)` fell through to the generic "not a keyword" branch and never decremented the level. So once any `(...)` pair appeared anywhere in a statement (e.g. a function signature `func(int)`), the split level stayed permanently elevated, and subsequent top-level semicolons stopped triggering statement splits — multiple statements merged into one (matching the reported "assert 1 == 2" failures for cases like psql dollar-quoted function bodies, issue83, issue193 splitting function, etc., which all involve parentheses before later semicolons).

Fix applied: changed the condition from `elif ttype is T.Punctuation and value != ')':` to `elif ttype is T.Punctuation and value == ')':` so the level only decreases on a genuine closing parenthesis, restoring correct paren-level tracking and semicolon-based statement splitting.

Verified with local repro scripts (since no test suite/tests directory is present in this checkout to run directly):
- Two plain statements still split correctly (2 statements).
- A statement followed by a line comment still splits correctly (2 statements).
- Two dollar-quoted `CREATE FUNCTION` statements with `(int)` parameter lists in their signatures, previously merged into 1 statement, now correctly split into 2.
